title: The broker instruction element, the case-move answer, the template price read and the auto-debit request have no published shape, and the broker fee and terms have no rule row, column set or value
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-034); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-24, R-DIS-25, R-DIS-26); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.25.3.1, A2.25.3.2); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1, T3.2, T5.1, appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slides 19, 24 and 43); Ownership Map v1; API Specification v4
description: (a) the request and answer properties of the Partner.issueInstruction activity are not specified anywhere although the activity name is given by Architecture v5 slides 19 and 24 and the typed-interface note of slide 24; (b) the rwb-case case-move answer has no published operation name or shape; (c) the rwb-comms template read has no operation name, and no source names the template code, the merge field or the binding that carries the buy-back price of R-DIS-24; (d) the rwb-payment auto-debit request of R-DIS-25 has no published operation name or shape; (e) the broker fee and the broker terms have no rule row: R-DIS-24 and R-DIS-25 are the buy-back and rental rules, and R-DIS-26, the broker rule, fixes the condition, the instruction and the state but carries no fee and no term, so no source gives the fee, its basis, its currency or the instruction term a value; (f) `listing` in TSD S5 T3.1 carries DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 with no fee or term property and `asset_sale` DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019 with sale fields only, so the fee and the terms have no column set in any source version; (g) the name of the step activity is a design choice that no source fixes.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-24, R-DIS-25 and R-DIS-26 (condition, action and to-state only, no fee or term); FSD S5 v3 A2.25.3.1 (R-DIS-24, R-DIS-25, R-DIS-26 and BR-S5-025) and A2.25.3.2 (the field catalog names v_ace_npa_asset and v_ace_collateral columns only); TSD S5 v2 T3.1 (`listing` DF-SAL-001 to DF-SAL-008 and `asset_sale` DF-SAL-009 to DF-SAL-019), T3.2 (LOV-SALE-CHANNEL with BROKER, LOV-LISTING), T5.1 (INT-11 SVAF, INT-12 AMIS, INT-13 RPS and INT-27 HOME.SCB, no broker interface) and appendix T-A.1 (API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 only); Architecture v5 slides 19 OUT and 24 note 2 (Partner.issueInstruction on rwb-partner, its worker writes its own schema); Ownership Map v1 (`template` owner P6, DF-REF-045 to DF-REF-051); API Specification v4 (no broker, template, auto-debit or case-move operation).
area: Contract surface and route data (rwb-asset, rwb-case, rwb-partner, rwb-comms, rwb-payment)
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-asset and solution architect, with the owners of rwb-case, rwb-partner, rwb-comms and rwb-payment
proposed: Declare the instruction as the S9 activity with an additive request and answer element and a placeholder property list, declare the case-move answer, the template read, the auto-debit request and the package read as consumed rows with placeholders, read the fee and the terms as route data with their version, and let the DB story of the service add the additive fee and terms columns under DP-15; write no business value anywhere.

title: The legacy feature is titled Sell through a broker while two of its four criteria are the buy-back and rental rules, and the broker route's own rule and state sit outside the rule table of the slice
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-032, RWB-E4-033, RWB-E4-034); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIS-24, R-DIS-25, R-DIS-26); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.25.3.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T4); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 (BR-030)
description: Legacy RWB-E4-034 is titled and described as the broker route, yet AC2 is R-DIS-24, the buy-back rule at the template price, and AC3 is R-DIS-25, the rental rule with the auto-debit. The broker route's own rule is R-DIS-26 (route = broker and asset_type in (commercial_property, land), to BROKER_INSTRUCTED) and it has no criterion of its own in this legacy key beyond AC1. R-DIS-25 is duplicated: legacy RWB-E4-033 carries the same criterion as its AC2, and the rental build is RWB-S5-E4033-APP's. R-DIS-24 is carried by no other legacy key: FEAT-AST-23 is RWB-E4-032's and its criteria test R-DIS-66. No source states whether the buy-back terms and the rental terms are built on this step or on the sibling stories' steps of the same AssetDisposalWorkflow, and no requirement text names the broker route.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-034 Acceptance criteria (AC1 broker route, AC2 R-DIS-24, AC3 R-DIS-25); legacy RWB-E4-032 AC2 (R-DIS-66) and RWB-E4-033 AC2 (R-DIS-25); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-DIS-24, R-DIS-25 and R-DIS-26; FSD S5 v3 A2.25.3.1 (the three rules of FEAT-AST-25) and the Requirements served table (REQ-S5-009 and REQ-S5-010, no broker requirement); Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-030 (the broker sale carries a recorded approval); TSD S5 v2 T4 (R-DIS-21 to R-DIS-25 tabled, the rest under and 47 more).
owner_role: Business analyst, solution architect and the rule owner in rwb-decision
proposed: Keep the four legacy criteria word for word on this story, table the two rows the criteria test (R-DIS-24 and R-DIS-25), name R-DIS-26 and its BROKER_INSTRUCTED state in prose, record that the rental build is RWB-S5-E4033-APP's on the same step, and let the rule owner confirm the step boundary of the three routes.

title: The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (Requirements served); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4 (REQ-S5-009, REQ-S5-010); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 (BR-030); plan split_plan.json
description: The FSD S5 requirements served table and BR-030 of the Epics 3 to 8 BRD carry REQ-S5-009 and REQ-S5-010 for the recorded approval of every exit from a held asset, and the split plan carries no requirement row for RWB-S5-E4034; the two stories cite the requirement from the FSD and the BRD and name the absence rather than leaving the table empty.
evidence: FSD S5 v3 Requirements served (REQ-S5-009 and REQ-S5-010, Must, E4); Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-030 (broker sale with a recorded approval, REQ-S5-009 and REQ-S5-010, FEAT-AST-21 to FEAT-AST-25, RWB-E4-030 to RWB-E4-034); Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S5-010; split_plan.json rows RWB-S5-E4034-APP and RWB-S5-E4034-CON with reqs empty.
proposed: Cite REQ-S5-010 from the FSD and BR-030, keep the plan unchanged, and let step D1 number the row; no story content changes.

title: The legacy Data, Endpoints and Screen tables name another owner's tables, two superseded asset paths and screen states the target list does not carry
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-034); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T3.1, T3.2); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slides 19, 29, 37, 41 and 45); Ownership Map v1; API Specification v4
description: The legacy Data table names recovery_case, v_ace_npa_sale, decision_log_entry, rule_row and template; in the target recovery_case is P3's, every v_ace_* view is P1's and is read only by rwb-source-data, decision_log_entry and rule_row are P7's and template is P6's, so this service reads none of them as a table. The legacy Endpoints table names GET /api/recovery/... assets/{assetId} and POST /api/recovery/... assets/{assetId}/listings, and both v2 asset paths are superseded by the business-key form; POST .../assets/{assetId}/valuations is rwb-valuation's under ASM-A6-api-6. The legacy Screen and states table lists SCR-23 states Draft, below limit, approved and published, while LOV-LISTING carries DRAFT, LIVE, UNDER_OFFER, SOLD and WITHDRAWN, so the states do not map one to one. The `asset` row the listing hangs from has no Ownership Map row although Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 and TSD S5 T3.1 give it to S5.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-034 Data, Endpoints and Screen and states tables; Ownership Map v1 (recovery_case and task owner P3; decision_log_entry, rule_row and approval owner P7; template owner P6; asset_sale and listing owner S5; POST /assets/{assetId}/valuations owner S1 under ASM-A6-api-6; GET /assets/{assetId} and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings superseded under ASM-A6-api-15; no `asset` row); Architecture v5 slides 19, 29, 37, 41 and 45; TSD S5 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; API Specification v4 (/assets and /assets/{assetKey}).
area: Data boundary, path ownership and screen states
proposed: Read the legacy rows as corrected: no v_ace_* read and no case, rule, template or partner row; the business-key asset paths; the SCR-23 states as the business conditions of the approval and the listing status of LOV-LISTING; and record the missing `asset` ownership row for the architect.

title: The listing path is the asset-id form in the Ownership Map, the TSD and the legacy story while API Specification v3 and v4 carry the business-key form
source: Ownership Map v1 (GET /assets/{assetId}, POST /assets/{assetId}/listings, ASM-A6-api-15); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (appendix T-A.1); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.25.3.2); Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 (/assets, /assets/{assetKey}); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-034)
description: API Specification v2 declares the asset paths with an assetId path parameter, and the Ownership Map rows GET /assets/{assetId} and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings carry that form with ASM-A6-api-15 recording that v3 supersedes them by the business-key path. API Specification v3 and v4 declare /assets and /assets/{assetKey}. TSD S5 appendix T-A.1 keeps the asset-id form (API-S5-001 to API-S5-005) and the legacy story's Endpoints table does too, while the FSD A2.25.3.2 says the listing and asset_sale link to the ACE asset_key by key with no foreign key and TSD S5 T3.1 keys `asset` by a uuid. No source reconciles the path parameter with a column of the table, so no source states how the business key resolves on the row.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 rows GET /assets/{assetId} and POST /assets/{assetId}/listings with ASM-A6-api-15, and POST /listings/{listingId}/rounds with no ruling; TSD S5 v2 appendix T-A.1 (API-S5-001 to API-S5-005 in the asset-id form); FSD S5 v3 A2.25.3.2 (v_ace_npa_asset.asset_key, no foreign key); API Specification v4 (/assets and /assets/{assetKey}); TSD S5 v2 T3.1 (asset id uuid, asset_ref varchar(20); listing asset_id uuid).
proposed: Declare the business-key form that API Specification v3 and v4 carry, keep API-S5-005 on the listing identifier, and record the correction of the two Ownership Map rows and of the TSD endpoint inventory as documentation acts rather than as a second contract.

title: The module event list gives rwb-asset one published event while the catalogue gives two
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slides 19 OUT, 41, 42 and 43); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T5.3); Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R3 R-PREC)
description: TSD S5 T5.3 lists AssetTakenOn as the module's only published event, while Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT and slide 43 give rwb.asset.events.v1 both AssetTakenOn (event 22) and AssetSold (event +). Under R-PREC the Architecture catalogue wins, so the service owns two events; neither of them is published by the broker route step, whose take-on sibling owns AssetTakenOn and whose sale story owns AssetSold. The two stories of this slice therefore declare no published and no consumed event and record the difference instead of resolving it.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT (rwb.asset.events.v1: AssetTakenOn, AssetSold), slide 41 (service table row S5) and slide 43 (event 22 and the AssetSold row); TSD S5 v2 T5.3 (AssetTakenOn published only); Template and Rules v1 R3 (Arch v5 catalogue first, the loser recorded as a Conflict gap and an assumption).
proposed: Declare that the service owns both events under the catalogue, that this step publishes neither, and record the correction of TSD S5 T5.3 for the sale story and the catalogue owner; no build of this slice changes.

title: No approval record, deprecation window or fake retention is stated for the contract baseline
source: Root AGENTS.md rules 1 to 14 and the D-RCV-60 overlay; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R1 U8, R9); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slide 42); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (appendix T-B)
description: The baseline sits in Draft (realignment v1) with no approval record and the run proceeds under the D-RCV-60 overlay, and no source fixes the deprecation window of a published property or the retention period of a contract fake, so both stay open for the solution architect while the baseline unblocks Day-1 work.
evidence: Root AGENTS.md rules 1 to 14 and the D-RCV-60 overlay (no human approval in this run; record an assumption and continue in Draft); Template and Rules v1 R1 U8 and R9 (no verification stop; gaps and assumptions); Architecture v5 slide 42 (BACKWARD compatibility and versioned schemas); TSD S5 v2 appendix T-B (DL06, DL11 and DL35 open).
proposed: Baseline in Draft, record the missing approval and the open deprecation window and fake retention as assumptions, and collect the consumer sign-off when it is available.

title: The rule package in force is pushed to four services and not to rwb-asset, and DP-04 is not in the pattern set of this key
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 (slides 19, 43 row 30 and 44 JOB-20); Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 (slides 15 and 16); Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R5.5 DP-04); Recovery Workbench TSD S5 Assets and auction v2 (T2, T4); Recovery Workbench FSD S5 Assets and auction v3 (A2.25.3.1)
description: The step evaluates R-DIS-24, R-DIS-25 and R-DIS-26 with the DISPOSAL package at its version in force, while Architecture v5 slide 43 row 30 lists rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment as the consumers of RulePackageInForce and not rwb-asset, slide 19 IN names no rule-package feed for the service, and DP-04 (RuleEvaluator and Drools, package from rwb-decision) is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key. No source states how the package reaches the evaluator of this service or which contract row carries its version.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 19 IN and OUT (no rule-package feed), slide 43 row 30 (RulePackageInForce consumers), slide 44 JOB-20 (Rule promote, rwb-decision); Temporal and Drools Design slides 15 and 16 (governance central, one KieBase per package version, the rule ID and version written to the record); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04 (H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON) against the pattern set of this key (DP03, DP05, DP13, DP19); TSD S5 v2 T2 (calls the rules component) and T4 (DISPOSAL, 72 rules).
owner_role: Solution architect and the rule owner in rwb-decision
proposed: Fetch the DISPOSAL package at its version in force on the rwb-decision package contract at the start of the step, hold it for the evaluation and write the package code and version to the decision record; declare the row as consumed and leave the plan's pattern set and the event catalogue unchanged.
